name: Gofish
headline: Mathematics master's student exploring Agent RSI and Physical AI.
intro: I do mathematics because I like problems that won't let me lie to myself. The rest of the time I'm on a mountain, in a kitchen, or on a badminton court.
heroCaption: The Dolomites. The fog cleared for about four minutes.
about: Hi, I'm Gofish. I'm studying for a master's in mathematics at Southern University of Science and Technology. Before that, I studied Mathematical Foundation Science at Dalian University of Technology.

Two questions I keep coming back to: how does an agent get better from its own experience? What does a model need to act in the world instead of only describing it? I don't have a thesis yet — that's what the next three years are for.
Away from a screen: badminton, cooking, film, and any mountain with a trail. I take cooking far too seriously for my skill level.

research.title: To lick, or not to lick?
research.subtitle: Kentucky Fried Chicken Original Recipe · Reinforcement learning
research.description: When should you lick your fingers while eating Kentucky Fried Chicken's Original Recipe chicken? I want to model grease buildup, cooling chicken and the reward of a lick, then compare licking after every bite, waiting until the end and adaptive policies. An advertising slogan becomes a sequential decision problem.

details.approach: Represent the state with grease, remaining chicken and temperature; choose to eat, lick or wipe. Solve a small model with dynamic programming, then see whether Q-learning approaches its optimal policy.
details.evaluation: Compare reward, time and accumulated discomfort under the same conditions, then vary preferences. Reward only grease actually removed, so endless licking cannot become a shortcut to a high score.

research.title: Is the middle bun a redundant token?
research.subtitle: McDonald's Big Mac · LLMs & structured ablation
research.description: Is a McDonald's Big Mac still a Big Mac with one less bun? Borrowing from context compression and ablation studies, I want to separate the middle bun’s contribution by quantity from its role in the stack, and test whether LLMs can predict the changes in taste and stability.

details.approach: Compare the original, middle-bun removal, an equal bread reduction from the outer buns and reordered layers. Ask an LLM to predict performance from ingredient descriptions and cross-section images before tasting.
details.evaluation: Rate flavor similarity, Big Mac identity, structural stability and personal preference separately, then compare them with model predictions. Tasting better and resembling the original are separate objectives.
